blocks.x: Revised FY27 Budget: SRO Costs Reallocated to the City
8.1 & 8.2 — Public Hearing on the Revised Budget Warrants
Discussion Summary

This special meeting existed for one purpose: formally reducing the FY27 school budget. The City Council had given first-reading approval (the first of two required votes) to moving the full cost of the district's School Resource Officer (SRO) program out of the school budget and into the City's public safety budget.
Chair Mancuso had requested this reallocation in writing from the City, as she reported at the April 8 Finance Committee meeting. No members of the public spoke at the hearing.
Key Decisions
8.1 (recess into public hearing): approved 6–0, unanimous. Moved by Erin Cavallaro, seconded by Noreen Poitras.
8.2 (close public hearing, return to session): approved 6–0, unanimous. Moved by Erin Cavallaro, seconded by Noreen Poitras.
Action Items
None.
8.3 — Adoption of the Revised FY27 Budget (First Reading, Roll Call Vote)
Discussion Summary
Chair Mancuso read the specific warrant revisions into the record. Warrant articles are separate budget questions approved by the Council and voters. The revisions touched three articles:
Article 3 (additional local funds) was reduced from $11,829,489.94 to $11,693,194.55.
Article 4 (total budget) was reduced from $57,349,321.39 to $57,213,026.00.
Article 4A (regular instruction) was reduced from $21,712,387.01 to $21,576,091.62.
Each reduction reflects the same $136,295.39. That is the school department's former 50% share of SRO salary and benefit costs, now reallocated entirely to the City's public safety budget.
Chair Mancuso publicly thanked City administration and the supportive members of the City Council for accommodating the change.
Key Decisions

Approved 6–0 by roll call (first reading); a second and final reading follows May 4, ahead of City Council's own second and final vote on the combined budget the same evening. Moved by Noreen Poitras, seconded by Katy Rice; unanimous.
Action Items
None.
